questions.question: What is the name of the central area in PicToBlox where our characters (sprites) move, dance, and play their games?
questions.explanation: Great job! The Stage is our magical virtual screen where sprites perform and game action comes to life.

questions.question: Which block allows you to make a character speak with a text bubble on the screen for a specific number of seconds?
options: motion: glide (1) secs to x:(0) y:(0)
questions.explanation: Correct! The 'say for () seconds' block shows a speech bubble above our sprite, then makes it disappear after the timer ends.

questions.question: If you want a racing sprite to slide smoothly across the screen from one place to another, which Motion block should you use?
questions.explanation: Amazing! The 'glide' block moves our sprite smoothly to the destination, whereas the 'go to' block jumps there instantly.

questions.question: How do we write code in PicToBlox?
options: By typing long text words on the keyboard
By dragging and snapping color blocks together like lego pieces
By drawing lines with a pencil on the screen
By talking to the computer microphone
questions.explanation: Perfect! In PicToBlox, we code by simply dragging colored blocks and linking them together to instruct our sprites.

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: Describe a block script to make a sprite glide smoothly to coordinates X = 150, Y = 150 in exactly 2 seconds.
questions.task_hint: Write: glide 2 secs to x: 150 y: 150
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Using the glide block and setting the time to 2 seconds makes the character slide beautifully.

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: Write the block name you would use to make a sprite play the sound 'cheering' when the game starts.
questions.explanation: Superb! The 'start sound' block plays cheerful sound effects to make your stories and games exciting.
